lines.text: Every answer from an artificial intelligence travels as light, through glass fibre.
Seven hundred and thirteen subsea cable systems carry that light between continents.
Only seven international cables land in Canada. The United States has eighty five, the United Kingdom fifty five, Singapore forty five, and Japan twenty eight.
Alberta has the power lines, the pipelines and the plants. Alberta has no coast, and no subsea cable lands here.
So how does intelligence made in Alberta reach the world? The route has to be planned across the whole country.
The Pan-Canadian Fibre Optics Planner is a map and route solver for planning that network.
The planner draws twenty three layers of public data on one globe. First come the corridors, the highways and the rail lines.
Next come the people and the land. The planner shows First Nations and Inuit communities, reserves, land claim areas and Métis Settlements.
In the North, the planner maps permafrost, and two hundred and seventy six remote communities that are off the main power grid.
Finally, the planner shows where providers report fibre today, and which communities have no fibre backbone nearby.
On that ground, the planner models fifteen routes. The southern route follows the Trans-Canada Highway from Victoria to St. John's, for seven thousand two hundred and sixty four kilometres.
The northern route runs from Prince Rupert to Churchill, with indicative subsea legs to Japan and Ireland.
A planner sets the waypoints and the weights. The solver searches the road and rail network, and returns the least cost path.
The planner compares three ways from Alberta to the Pacific, by length, by crossings and by the land each route passes.
Where no road or rail exists, a planner draws a line. The estimate gives an indicative cost range.
The plan is for an integrated Canada, where our natural resources and capabilities serve communities coast to coast.
Alberta can be the world's source for intelligence.
Connecting to our partners across Canada and globally provides a promising future for Alberta innovation to power the world.
